title: Umm Salamah
hook: her counsel breaks a silence at Hudaybiyyah, and her question is answered by a verse of the Qur'an

segments.voice: Yesterday, Hafsah and the sheets that came back to her house. Your line was: she kept the pages. What did you put somewhere safe? Day eight hundred eleven.

Nobody moves. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, has just agreed a treaty at Hudaybiyyah, outside Mecca, and the terms feel to his companions like a defeat. He tells them: get up, sacrifice your animals, and shave your heads. Bukhari says not one of them rose. He says it again. And again. Silence. So he goes into his tent, to his wife, and tells her what has happened. Today: Umm Salamah.
screen: `A TREATY THAT FEELS LIKE DEFEAT.` → `NOT ONE OF THEM ROSE.` → `HE GOES IN TO HIS WIFE.`

segments.voice: Her advice, in Bukhari, is short and wise. Go out, she says, and don't say a word to anyone. Sacrifice your own animal, and call your barber to shave your head. He does exactly that. And when the companions see it, they get up, sacrifice, and start shaving one another, crowding so hard in their distress that it looked as if they might hurt each other. Umm Salamah understood something about grief and pride: people who won't be argued into moving can sometimes be shown. That's the first thing she's remembered for: counsel in a hard hour. The second is a question. In a report in the Musnad of Ahmad, Umm Salamah asks the Prophet: why are we, the women, not mentioned in the Qur'an the way the men are? She doesn't say it in a corner. She asks him directly. And then, the report says, she heard him reciting from the pulpit a new verse, surah thirty-three, verse thirty-five. In Pickthall it begins: "Lo! men who surrender unto Allah, and women who surrender". And it goes on like that, pair after pair: men who believe and women who believe, men who are truthful and women who are truthful, men who give charity and women who give charity, men who fast and women who fast, all the way to forgiveness and a vast reward. The verse speaks to women and men alike. The report adds a story behind it: someone asked. Her question didn't ask for less from women. It asked to be named. She asked, and it came.
screen: `GO OUT AND SAY NOTHING.` · `SACRIFICE, AND THEY ALL FOLLOW.` · `WHY ARE WE NOT MENTIONED?` · `MEN WHO SURRENDER, AND WOMEN WHO SURRENDER.` · then, large: `SHE ASKED, AND IT CAME.`

segments.voice: The practice: ask the question that's missing. Settle, and breathe. Think of a room you're part of: a family, a team, a congregation, a class. Is there someone, or something, nobody ever mentions there? Let the question form, as plainly as Umm Salamah's: why isn't this spoken of? You don't have to ask it yet. Just find the words, and hold them. If you pray, you can bring that question to Allah, as she brought hers to the Prophet. The bell holds the time.
Umm Salamah. The mother of the believers whose counsel moved the silent camp at Hudaybiyyah, and whose question is linked to the verse that names women and men side by side. Today's word.
Your line: she asked, and it came. Today, ask your missing question out loud, kindly, to someone who can answer it. Day eight hundred eleven.

howItsDone: Muslims recite surah 33:35 as a verse naming believing men and women side by side, and retell Umm Salamah's advice at Hudaybiyyah from Sahih al-Bukhari as an example of wise counsel.

pairs: men and women named side by side

myth: the companions obeyed at once at Hudaybiyyah
Bukhari says none rose though he told them three times.
Umm Salamah advised him to act without speaking
she told him to sacrifice and shave, saying nothing, and they followed.
Umm Salamah asked why women weren't mentioned like the men
the report in Ahmad links her question to surah 33:35.

fork.setup: you are the Prophet's wife. he tells you his companions won't move after the treaty, though he asked three times. what do you advise?
options: tell him to command them again, more strongly.
tell him to say nothing, and sacrifice and shave himself.
tell him to wait a day until they calm down.
fork.reveal: in Bukhari she says: go out, speak to no one, sacrifice and call your barber. when they saw him, they all did the same.

original.note: Arabic: 'mother of Salamah', named after her son; her own name was Hind.

trapdoor: what you thought: one of the Prophet's wives, not much more.
what it means: a counselor whose advice moved a silent camp, and a questioner linked to a verse naming women and men together.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari 2731–2732 for Hudaybiyyah; Musnad Ahmad (and al-Nasa'i's al-Sunan al-Kubra) for her question and 33:35.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732 (Hudaybiyyah; none rose; Umm Salamah's advice)
Musnad Ahmad 26575 (Umm Salamah asks why women are not mentioned; 33:35 recited from the pulpit)

sources.quoted: Lo! men who surrender unto Allah, and women who surrender

notes: Confirm the Pickthall wording of the opening of 33:35 word for word; the rest of the verse is paraphrased.
Musnad Ahmad number and the pulpit detail cited from memory; confirm, and confirm grading of the report.
'So eager that it looked as if they might hurt each other' paraphrases Bukhari's description; confirm.
'Her own name was Hind' (original game note): confirm.

Editor: corrected 'so eager' at Hudaybiyyah (Bukhari describes the companions as distressed, not eager); 'great reward' changed to Pickthall's 'vast reward'; cut the sweeping 'Muslims read the verse as speaking to everyone'; fixed the garbled 'adds a door to it'.
